title: RISC-V Ratified Specifications Library
strengths: Current ratified ISA and privileged truth; stable January 2026 core release
limitations: Too dense to serve as the main student teaching surface
notes: Use bounded excerpts/references with attribution; author student bridge

title: RISC-V ABIs Specification
strengths: Calling convention ELF and DWARF truth
limitations: Far deeper than Week 6 needs
notes: Use only the calling-convention/ELF pieces needed to interpret compiler output

title: RISC-V ISA Manual source
strengths: Attributable source for the open ISA manual
limitations: Specification-first rather than sophomore-first
notes: Preserve attribution when adapting

title: MIT OCW 6.004 Computation Structures
strengths: Coherent structural principles from logic through CPU memory pipelines and parallelism
limitations: Uses its own architecture and is older than our RISC-V-centered course; adapted content carries SA obligations
notes: Best broad adaptable OER ingredient; do not clone the course

title: MIT 6.004 Labs
strengths: Strong bounded build/trace design ideas
limitations: Different architecture/tooling and too much to transplant directly
notes: Use lab-design ideas and author SWOSU-native experiences

title: UC Berkeley CS61C 2026 Course Notes
strengths: Excellent current explanations of representation RISC-V CPU pipeline caches performance and VM
limitations: NoDerivatives means link/cite only; notes are still actively developed
notes: Do not derive our lecture prose or figures from these notes

title: UC Berkeley CS61C 2026 course site
strengths: Current sequencing projects labs and modern coverage
limitations: Artifact licensing varies and workload/prerequisites are heavier than SWOSU target
notes: Inspect license per artifact; use primarily as benchmark

title: Cornell CS3410 Spring 2026
strengths: Current integrated text-note/lab sequence spanning C RISC-V CPU caches OS and parallelism
limitations: No broad reuse license identified; assumes stronger C/systems context than some students
notes: Link; do not copy assignments or notes without license

title: Cornell CS3410 RISC-V Infrastructure
strengths: Concrete Docker plus GCC plus QEMU RISC-V path with Windows WSL macOS and Linux instructions
limitations: Course-specific image and commands should not be cloned blindly
notes: Strong evidence for Prompt 003 architecture-lab feasibility

title: Cambridge Introduction to Computer Architecture 2025-26
strengths: Excellent RISC-V-to-GPU coverage and architecture scope check
limitations: Some detailed handouts are cam.ac.uk-domain restricted and public access does not imply reuse rights
notes: Use as coverage/practical benchmark rather than required spine

title: Cambridge RISC-V Practical / Clarvi
strengths: Small understandable RV32I core using Spike plus cycle-accurate simulation
limitations: SystemVerilog/FPGA depth exceeds our one-week CPU build target
notes: Useful proof that a small real RISC-V core can bridge ISA and implementation

title: Nand2Tetris Project 5 / course
strengths: Makes CPU memory and complete computer parts acquire meaning through construction
limitations: Hack ISA and project sequence differ from RISC-V course; instructional reuse rights not assumed
notes: Preserve build-the-machine instinct without importing the full Hack curriculum

title: Nand2Tetris simulator source
strengths: Open simulation tooling and useful implementation reference
limitations: GPL integration/distribution consequences if bundled
notes: Tool license is separate from instructional-content rights

title: Linux kernel /proc documentation
strengths: Direct documentation for process maps memory state and machine observation
limitations: Kernel configuration and permissions affect what fields students can see
notes: Use with a course-owned Machine Telescope card

title: GNU GDB Documentation
strengths: Registers memory breakpoints and stepping are directly observable
limitations: Official manual is too large for beginner-first reading
notes: Course provides exact command subset

title: GNU Binutils/readelf Documentation
strengths: ELF and binary inspection truth
limitations: Tool reference rather than conceptual explanation
notes: Use through guided command recipes

title: GCC RISC-V Options
strengths: Compiler ISA ABI and vector-target option truth
limitations: Many flags are irrelevant to the course
notes: Prompt 003/004 should pin only required flags

title: QEMU User Mode Emulation
strengths: Runs programs compiled for another CPU architecture on the host OS
limitations: Emulation is not equivalent to hardware performance and must not be benchmarked as such
notes: Strong execution path for instruction-level work

title: QEMU RISC-V System Emulator
strengths: Emulates 32-bit and 64-bit RISC-V systems
limitations: System emulation adds board/device complexity not needed for every lab
notes: Likely enrichment or selected Week 11 use rather than default for all students

title: Docker Get Started / Concepts
strengths: Clear image/container/runtime concepts and mainstream setup guidance
limitations: Vendor/runtime-specific; course should remain Podman/Docker aware where practical
notes: Teach reproducibility rather than Docker trivia

title: Matplotlib stable documentation
strengths: Stable Python plotting foundation with exportable figures
limitations: Raw API surface is much larger than students need
notes: Course owns plotting helpers; plotting syntax is not graded

title: Tectonic Typesetting System
strengths: Modern MIT-licensed TeX engine aimed at reproducible builds
limitations: Bundled/downloaded TeX assets have their own licenses and Prompt 003 must validate install size/platform behavior
notes: Strong candidate for one-command Machine Dossier PDF

title: OpenMP Specifications
strengths: Portable shared-memory parallel model with current OpenMP 6.0 spec
limitations: Full specification is far too large for student-first reading
notes: Use a tiny subset through course-owned examples

title: OpenMP Examples 6.0.1
strengths: Current free examples covering parallel execution SIMD synchronization and more
limitations: Still broader than course needs and syntax can distract from architecture
notes: Better teaching companion than assigning the full spec

title: Open MPI Documentation
strengths: Officially supports multi-process MPI jobs on one laptop/workstation
limitations: Installation and MPI syntax may add friction; local shared-memory MPI does not reproduce a real network by itself
notes: Optional communication instrument if Prompt 003 proves humane

title: NVIDIA CUDA Programming Guide
strengths: Current official SIMT memory hierarchy coalescing and data-movement explanations
limitations: Vendor-specific and GPU hardware is not available to every student
notes: Instructor/optional student truth source; CPU-only lab remains canonical

title: PCPartPicker System Builder
strengths: Familiar build workflow combining parts compatibility and current retail observations
limitations: Aggregator is not architecture truth; compatibility coverage and prices must be independently checked where material
notes: Recommended default exercise surface with equivalent alternatives allowed

title: Week 5/14 current manufacturer and retailer evidence
strengths: Lets students compare real current components prices capacities power and interfaces
limitations: Volatile and vendor-specific; URLs/products change
notes: Date-stamp every observation; verify specifications against manufacturer pages where practical

title: Shared SWOSU Success Foundations
strengths: Keeps Week 1 aligned across the course family
limitations: Depends on shared-source readiness
notes: Reuse rather than fork

title: Shared AI Fluency / Professional Minds
strengths: Provides consistent AI Fluency and Professional Minds cadence
limitations: Architecture-specific application still must be authored
notes: Provider-neutral; no premium AI dependency

title: Shared Farkle + ML package
strengths: Preserves family-wide shared application/fun week
limitations: Not yet a reason to reopen Architecture technical content
notes: No Architecture capstone/checkpoint layer
